numerical_failure.observed_behavior: np.asarray(pd.NaT).astype('datetime64') raises TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer, because pd.NaT's year/month/day attributes return float('nan') and PyLong_AsLong fails on the year.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The conversion should produce a NaT datetime64 value instead of raising, e.g. array('NaT', dtype='datetime64[us]') as stated in the PR's 'After the fix' output.
trigger_conditions: input is pd.NaT (pandas NaT-like object whose year attribute is float NaN)
downstream call such as matplotlib pl.plot(pd.NaT, pd.NaT) hits the same failure

input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer

numerical_characteristics.dtype: datetime64 (M8[ns] in the explicit-unit test case; unitless astype('datetime64') in the bug-report case)
numerical_characteristics.precision: datetime64[ns] for the explicit-unit case; no unit given (generic unit, which emits a DeprecationWarning) for the bug-report case
category_specific_evidence: The special value involved is NaN, carried in the year, month and day attributes of a NaT-like object (e.g. pandas NaT); the test class NaTLike sets all three to float('nan').
Original failure: np.asarray(pd.NaT).astype('datetime64') raises TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer (issue#31608).

Correct handling per the test: the NaN-attribute object converts to NaT, so np.isnat(...) is True, for np.asarray(NaTLike(), dtype=object).astype('datetime64[ns]'), for np.datetime64(NaTLike(), 'ns'), and for the unitless astype('datetime64').

The fix in convert_pyobject_to_datetime checks dts.year == NPY_DATETIME_NAT and, when meta->base == NPY_FR_ERROR, sets the base to NPY_FR_GENERIC with num=1, bypassing unit cast-safety checks as NaT scalars do.
The unitless case must emit DeprecationWarning matching "The 'generic' unit for NumPy datetime is deprecated".
Inf, signed zero and subnormals are not mentioned in any passage.
reproduction_risks: The unitless case raises a DeprecationWarning, so a reproduction that treats warnings as errors will fail there.
The test relies on duck-typed NaN attributes rather than a real pandas NaT; behaviour with real pandas NaT is only described in the PR text.
The passages give no numeric tolerance; NaT checks use np.isnat rather than a tolerance comparison.
